Pap Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kossuth út 58, Hungary

Not demolished. Pap's Jewish presence dates to the end of the 18th century, when 8 people — Sámuel Dávid and his relatives — lived on the estate of István Fülöp; the population peaked at 76 in 1910 before declining to 41 by 1941. The community's oldest families were the Kaufman, Kohn, Dicker, and Schmilovics families, engaged mainly as merchants, cobblers, and landowners; prayer services were held in the house of Béni Kohn in the early 20th century. A local resident, Bernát Frenkel, died in 1942 in forced labor service on a Russian battlefield; the rest of the community was deported via the Kisvárda Ghetto to Auschwitz in 1944. Only 2 Jews remained in Pap by 1949, and they too left by 1956. This cemetery was established as early as 1870, per that year's cadastral map, remaining in use until at least 1942.
